newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto approves state banks merger.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto approves state banks merger.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto has approved moves to merge the country's state banks to improve their competitiveness, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Friday.
"Suharto has been fully informed and principally he agrees on such a move (to merge state banks)," Mar'ie told reporters after meeting Suharto.
"What is left now is the technical details on which banks will be merged. There is a possibility affiliated banks could emerge. That's also possible. We are preparing it (the policy)," Mar'ie said.
The minister said it would take some time to finalise details, but gave no time-frame.
The World Bank said in a recent report that Indonesia needed to improve its financial institutions to meet possible macroeconomic shocks.

The bank suggested interim measures were needed to improve state banks' corporate governance and performance such as closures, mergers and downsizing, perhaps in conjunction with the spinoff and sale of some of their activities. Bisnis Indonesia daily reported earlier the government planned to merge its seven state banks into four entities.
It said PT Bank Negara Indonesia, PT Bank Expor Impor Indonesia, PT Bank Dagang Negara and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia would emerge from the consolidation.
